newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
MOVE AFOOT TO EXTEND CENTRAL RULE IN UTTAR PRADESH

The government was expected to introduce a resolution in parliament seeking a six-month extension of president's rule in Uttar Pradesh state. The government was making efforts to get the resolution passed by both houses before parliament closes for a four-week recess, beginning on March 22. The ruling United Front issued a three-line whip to its members to vote in support of the official resolution for the extension of president's rule in Uttar Pradesh.
The Hindustan Times
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY TO PRESS FOR VOTING ON MOTION

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), spurning the overtures of the ruling United Front (UF), decided to take its motion for the recall of the Uttar Pradesh governor to its logical conclusion. Amid speculation of a deal being worked out by the UF's intermediaries, BJP sources said nothing short of the governor's recall would satisfy the party. Settling for anything less would throw up a credibility crisis, party leaders admitted.
Indian Express
MUTINOUS STATE UNITS PIN DOWN CONGRESS CHIEF

Panic gripped the Congress party following reports from various states that the party president's writ no longer ran unchallenged, even in organisational matters. The signs of rebellion added to the party chief's woes, coming at a time when Maharashtra strongman Sharad Pawar was trying to prevent the former from imposing his political agenda on the parliamentary party and determine the party's relationship with the ruling United Front.
The Economic Times
GOVERNMENT MAY VALIDATE PETROL PUMP, HOUSE ALLOTMENTS

The government initiated a move for revalidating the controversial allotment of petrol pumps and government houses made by two former ministers. A proposal for getting allotments, which were cancelled by the Supreme Court following charges of grave irregularities, was put up before the cabinet. The proposal, which suggested either reviewing the allotments or a legislation for legalising them, sought to undo the apex court's work. A decision was deferred as some cabinet members felt the need to take opposition parties into confidence over the move.
VOLTAS CHIEF QUITS OVER POOR RESULTS

Voltas chief executive and managing director Vishwanath Munshi resigned from his position, accepting responsibility for the recent performance of the 11.4 billion rupee company. Munshi attributed Voltas's performance to the downturn in the refrigerators and washing machines segments and the company's failure to revive the sick Hyderabad Allwyn unit. Voltas reported a 49 million rupee net loss for the six months ended September 30, 1996, compared to a 124.9 million rupee profit in the corresponding period of the previous year.
TAX CUTS NOT TO BOOST COLLECTION: ECONOMISTS

Several economists expressed doubts that lower tax rates would yield the desired increase in revenue collection. The point was made at a brainstorming session on the budget organised by an industry body. They said the tax rates were reduced too much and felt the logic of reducing tax rates in the hope of generating revenue was suspect. Apprehensions were also expressed that tax breaks might result in a decline in savings over the coming years.
DO AWAY WITH CREDIT RATIONING: EXPERT PANEL

An expert panel set up by the Indian Banks' Association suggested scrapping the prescribed uniform formula for maximum permissible bank finance (MPBF). It advocated banks should have the sole discretion to determine borrowing limits of corporates. However, members of the committee differed over whether the MPBF concept should be completely done away with and how the changeover to a new system should be made.
NORSK HYDRO BIDS TO TURN AROUND MANGALORE CHEMICALS

Norsk Hydro, one of the world's largest fertiliser companies, offered to turn around Vijay Mallaya's sick Mangalore Chemicals and Fertilisers (MCF). This was the first time the $13 billion group showed interest in setting up its own fertiliser manufacturing facility in India. Sources said Norsk Hydro was prepared to set up a new joint venture company with Indian partners for making fertilisers in the country if it failed to acquire MCF.
Financial Express
SIMOCO PICKS 51 PCT STAKE IN PHILIPS TELECOM

Britain's Simoco acquired a 51 percent stake in Philips Telecommunications Industries (PTIL), Calcutta, one of the largest mobile wireless communications company. The remaining 49 percent of PTIL would be bought over by Simoco in the coming year. The new company to be formed as a result of this acquisition would be named Simoco South Asia.
E MERCK GETS GO-AHEAD FOR 100 PCT SUBSIDIARY

German multinational E Merck received clearance to set up a 100 percent subsidiary, Merck Development Centre, in India. Similar proposals by other drug giants like Pfizer have been turned down in the recent past. The new company, set up for development research, would focus on bulk drugs and formulations. The venture would entail an initial investment of 150 million rupees and was expected to be operational by late 1998.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS DENIED TAX BENEFITS

Financial institutions (FIs) will not be able to claim a tax benefit on the entire amount of write-offs of bad debt any more. The Finance Bill 1997 would force all public FIs as well as state financial corporations and state industrial investment corporations to pay taxes on the written-off amount with retrospective effect from April 1992. Institutions such as banks would be allowed to claim tax benefits on the written off amount that exceeded the provisioning of bad debt. The proposed amendment would bring FIs on par with banks in regard to tax benefits on provisioning and write-off of bad debt, tax experts said.
EXPORT SCHEMES MERGER MAY BE SPIKED

The Commerce Ministry was unlikely to press the government for merging several existing export promotion schemes into two viable ones. The ministry had proposed the merger to ensure their effective implementation in the new five-year export-import policy. It would, however, strive to rationalise the long-winding procedures attendant with these schemes. The proposal reportedly did not receive the backing of the panel set up by the government to frame the new export-import policy to be effective from April 1, 1997.
Business Standard
CORPORATES WARNED AGAINST POSTPONING TAX PAYMENT

The government will come down heavily on corporates who postpone tax payments due on March 15 to the next quarter to take advantage of tax cuts proposed in the budget. Advance tax rules require corporate tax to be paid in four instalments. On March 15, they have to pay 25 percent of corporate tax and 40 percent of income tax as advance payments. The revenue secretary clarified that accounting is on an accrual basis and therefore it is not possible for corporates to postpone payments to the first quarter of the next financial year.
FINANCE MINISTRY WANTS COGENTRIX TO REWORK AGREEMENT

The Finance Ministry wants the promoters of the Mangalore power project to rework the power purchase agreement. The promoters are Cogentrix Inc of the United States and China Light and Power International. Cogentrix officials have conveyed their dismay over further delay in clearance. The government has already agreed to the counter guarantee of the project, subject to the agreement being approved by the Finance Ministry.
AMBANIS' BID TO HIKE FOREIGN EQUITY IN MUDRA TO 74 PCT

Mudra Communications sought clearance to hike its foreign equity to 74 percent from 10 percent. Its promoters, the Ambanis, sought permission to include a blanket enabling provision which would allow a foreign equity increase in Mudra. But the Ambanis would retain the blocking vote on the company board with their remaining 26 percent stake. Measures considered to raise foreign equity include tapping the overseas capital markets with a global depository receipts issue and a long-term bond issue. Offloading a part of the shareholding in favour of joint venture partner DDB Needham of Britain, was also being considered.
ENTHUSIASTIC RESPONSE TO VSNL ISSUE

Roadshows for Videsh Sanchar Nigam's global depository receipts issue, which moved to London, continued to evoke a strong response. Co-lead managers to the issue claimed it was already fully subscribed. Target selling over the past two days with key investors at Hong Kong, Singapore and Tokyo was done in the 850-950 rupee range, which was seen as extremely lucrative by investors.
The Observer
BID TO EASE INCOME TAX MAY BOOMERANG

Some of the changes suggested by the expert panel to rationalise and simplify income tax laws would not serve the purpose of devising a sound tax structure. Instead they would result in unhealthy consequences, a member of the panel which submitted its report to the Finance Ministry said. Meanwhile, a senior tax official submitted a dissent note expressing his reservations over some of the recommendations.
BUYBACK OF SHARES WITHOUT RIGHTS OPPOSED

A recommendation of the working group on the Companies Act was opposed by corporates. The working group proposed that the buyback of shares through treasury operations route would not have voting rights until the shares were reissued. Besides, the bought-back shares would also not be eligible for dividend rights, bonus shares as well as rights issue. Companies feared the proposition would weaken the hedge against hostile takeover bids. The recommendations were currently being considered by the government.
